newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dow's grim start hits SAfrica industrials at close.
newsitem.headline: Dow's grim start hits SAfrica industrials at close.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended weak on Friday after taking a fright from Wall Street which fell more than 100 points shortly after the opening, dealers said.
Wall Street's slide jolted the industrial index to end off 30.8 points at 9,283.4, while the all-shares shed 15.2 points to close at 7,599.2.
Dealers said the fall also spurred more profit-taking which had gripped the industrials during most of the day, epitomised by a surge in local and foreign buying interest.
Turnover was 1.3 billion rand compared to 1.9 billion rand on Thursday as 36 shares surged to new highs and 10 fell to new lows.
In the broader market, decliners led advancers by 189 to 185.
A slightly better bullion price, holding firm as bullion pushed its head above $320 and ounce helped resuscitate golds which have grimaced amid current bullion woes at lower levels.
The gold index added 29.3 points to 996.4.
Dealers said the market's underlying sentiment remained positive on hopes of an imminent interest rate cut with next week's trading seen continuing firm, provided the rand did not weaken further.
